summary: We made a fun space game for young children that tells the stories of things NASA left behind in space. A friendly squirrel astronaut named Bondoka guides the children through the game. They explore the planets, hear the stories, take a quiz, and even suggest their own ideas for these forgotten objects. It matters because children learn that space exploration leaves real traces, and that learning about them can be exciting instead of boring. That's why we worked so hard on this project
details:
Our project is a four-level space game for school-age children. In Level 1, children learn about the planets and the Moon. In Level 2, they explore a moving solar system, and our squirrel astronaut Bondoka tells short stories about things NASA left in space. Level 3 is a quiz, and in Level 4, children propose a solution for an abandoned object or research a space object. They win a prize after each level and get a certificate at the end.

Our goal is to make children curious about space and show them that every mission leaves something behind, and each thing has a story. We built it mostly with HTML, with CSS in a separate file for the design, and it works on laptops
